clue.text: Handle crew Silver assembled before start of expedition

parts.note: to crew a ship is to man it
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: the start of the word expedition supplies just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A pirate captain gathers his crew under Long John Silver before an expedition sets off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silver' looks like Long John Silver from Treasure Island, but it is just the metal's symbol AG; 'assembled' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To handle a situation or business is to run or cope with it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: It is said to impart confidence in the theatre

definitions.text: It is said to impart confidence in the theatre

parts.words: It is said to impart confidence in the theatre
parts.note: on stage, an actor speaks a line meant for the audience alone, sharing a confidence, that is a secret, rather than boosting anyone's self-assurance

explanation.surface: Something spoken on stage that gives performers self-belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confidence' reads as self-assurance, but here it means a secret shared: a remark the other characters supposedly cannot hear.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage remark addressed to the audience, unheard by the other characters, is a theatrical convention for sharing a secret.

clue.text: A solitary retainer on an eastern vessel

parts.note: an anchor retains or holds a ship in place
SS stands for steamship, a vessel

explanation.surface: A lone servant travels aboard a ship bound for the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retainer' suggests a servant, but it is the thing that holds a ship still; 'solitary' is a noun here, a recluse.
explanation.definitionFit: A female religious recluse who lived walled up in a cell was a medieval kind of hermit.

clue.text: Told off Head — and very pleased about it

indicators.note: taking off the head of a word removes its first letter

parts.note: to have told a story is to have related it

explanation.surface: Someone was reprimanded by the headteacher and is rather smug about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Told off' reads as scolded, but 'off Head' is the deletion signal: RELATED loses its first letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thrilled or overjoyed about something is a direct synonym for this feeling.

clue.text: It's party time, note — throw off all restraint

parts.note: Lib is short for the Liberal party
an era is a period of time
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: It's party time: a cue to let loose and abandon all inhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints letting one's hair down at a party; 'throw off all restraint' means to free, set loose.
explanation.definitionFit: To set free is to remove every shackle or constraint, so the phrase works as a synonym.

clue.text: Short of weight fighter has a late build-up

indicators.note: the letters are built up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A boxer who is under the weight limit tries to bulk up late before the weigh-in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'build-up' reworks FIGHTER HAS A LATE into the answer; the surface's fighter is a boxer failing to make weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something weighing almost nothing is described with this idiom of extreme lightness.

clue.text: Disreputable fellows in low area adjoining the East End

parts.note: base means low and dishonourable
men are fellows

indicators.note: the end of the word East is its final letter

explanation.surface: Seedy characters loiter in a run-down district next to London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the East End' looks like the London district, but 'End' simply picks the last letter of 'East', T.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest storey of a house, below ground level, is literally a low area.

clue.text: Sculptor of boy embracing girl

indicators.note: one name holds the other within its arms, so it goes around it

parts.note: Ron is a boy's name
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A sculpture shows a boy hugging a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the surface evokes the famous French sculptor's work The Kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste, the French artist behind The Thinker, was a celebrated sculptor.

clue.text: Transfer pad in turn for this kind of cricket

indicators.note: the letters are transferred into a different order

explanation.surface: A cricketer hands over his batting pad when his turn comes.
explanation.walkthrough: This is an informal form of cricket in which the batter must run whenever bat touches ball.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a casual variety of the bat-and-ball game, so it is an example of a kind of cricket.

clue.text: Pays cashiers

explanation.surface: Bank tellers are paid.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is settles a debt; the other is dismisses from the armed forces, as an officer is cashiered.

clue.text: Underworld boss collecting money from pickpockets

indicators.note: the god gathers the coin into himself, so it goes inside

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god who rules the underworld
p stands for penny or pence, money

explanation.surface: A gangland boss takes his cut from the pickpockets who work for him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld boss' suggests a mafia chief, but it is the Roman god of the dead; 'dips' is slang for pickpockets.
explanation.definitionFit: Dip is slang for a thief who picks pockets, from dipping a hand in.

clue.text: Recalling gift in split wrapping

indicators.note: the tear goes around the gift like paper around a present

parts.note: a rent is a tear or split
a dole is a charitable gift or handout

explanation.surface: Remembering a present inside torn wrapping paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a torn parcel, but 'Recalling' is the definition, as in 'redolent of', and 'wrapping' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being evocative of something, as in 'redolent of the past', means bringing it to mind.

clue.text: Performing operations to remove veins, perhaps?

definitions.text: Performing operations to remove veins, perhaps?

parts.words: Performing operations to remove veins, perhaps?
parts.note: it reads like vascular surgery, but the veins are seams of ore extracted from the ground by digging operations

explanation.surface: A surgeon carries out procedures to strip varicose veins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operations' and 'veins' suggest surgery; the veins are mineral deposits and the operations are underground workings.
explanation.definitionFit: Extracting ore or coal from seams in the earth is the work of the extraction industry.

clue.text: Teacher's inner longing

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the word Teacher's

explanation.surface: A teacher's private yearning.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a yearning for something is to feel a craving, a synonym of longing.

clue.text: Could be 7, the cheat

explanation.surface: A sculptor might also be a swindler.
explanation.definitionFit: Rodin worked with a chisel, so he is one who chisels stone; the word is also slang for a swindler who cheats people.

clue.text: At home in sheltered and comfortable position

indicators.note: one word is put inside the other

parts.note: secure means safe or sheltered
in means at home

explanation.surface: Snug and safe at home in a cosy spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At home' and 'in' look like one idea, but the first supplies letters and the second, 'in', is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushy job that pays well for little work is an easy, comfortable post.

clue.text: Conveyance in port secured by chain? Exactly!

indicators.note: the port is held within the chain

parts.note: a cable is a heavy chain, as for an anchor
Rio de Janeiro is a port
to a T means exactly

explanation.surface: A ship's cargo is fastened in harbour by an anchor chain, just so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exactly' gives T from the phrase 'to a T'.
explanation.definitionFit: A light horse-drawn carriage, or a convertible car, is a means of transport.

clue.text: Reserved performance includes re-written Act 1

indicators.note: the performance contains the rearranged letters

parts.note: a turn is an act or performance on stage

indicators.note: the letters are written again in a new order

parts.note: the numeral 1 is I in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A low-key show incorporates a revised first act.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan prints 'Act 1', the Roman numeral one, which the held text misread as an exclamation mark; 're-written' is the anagram signal and 'includes' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A taciturn person says little, keeping their thoughts to themselves, which is being reserved.

clue.text: List score lines for court official

parts.note: to list is to lean or tip over, as a ship lists
a staff is the set of five lines on which music is scored

explanation.surface: A clerk lists the scorelines for a court official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'List' suggests a register, but it means tilt; 'score lines' are the stave of written music.
explanation.definitionFit: A court usher or bailiff once carried a metal-tipped staff, giving this legal official his title.

clue.text: Plant covering new arch

indicators.note: the word for plant surrounds the letter for new

parts.note: to bed plants is to plant them

explanation.surface: A climbing plant grows over a newly built archway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' is a verb meaning to set in, giving BED, which goes around N.
explanation.definitionFit: To arch something is to curve or bow it, so the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: In fright slip under sheet at last

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece under another follows it
the word sheet supplies only its final letter

parts.note: a slip is a mistake

explanation.surface: In a panic, someone slips beneath the bedsheet at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' places ERROR below T in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme fear or dread is a stronger word for a fright.

clue.text: Sign giving information to one circling motorway

indicators.note: the information goes around the motorway

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI
one is I as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A road sign gives directions to a driver going round the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: THE M1 is the main British motorway north from London; 'circling' is the container signal, and 'Sign' means a sign of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: The Twins are a zodiac sign, so this is an example of a sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: First-class climbing requiring doctors for the feet

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing reads the letters upwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, read as the letters A and I
MB is a medical degree, so MBs are doctors

explanation.surface: Top-class mountaineering needs doctors to look after climbers' feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns A1 upwards to give IA; the feet are metrical, not anatomical.
explanation.definitionFit: In poetry these are metrical units of an unstressed then stressed syllable, so they are examples of feet.

clue.text: Sole in a saucy case provided as a starter

indicators.note: the single letter goes inside the case

parts.note: pert means saucy, and serves as the case holding the letter
sole means single, one, which is I
if means provided that

explanation.surface: Dover sole in a rich sauce served as an appetiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole' looks like the fish, but it means one, I; 'case' marks PERT as the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink taken before a meal to whet the appetite is a starter of sorts.

clue.text: Unskilful writer is sent up in it

indicators.note: the turned pen goes inside the word it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down entry, sent up reads the word upwards

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A clumsy author gets mocked in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' suggests mockery, but it reverses the writing tool to NEP; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Clumsy and lacking skill or competence is the meaning, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Prize fruit

explanation.surface: A prize-winning fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A choice job or reward is a plum one; it is also a stone fruit.

clue.text: Held under a new order without warning

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is detained under a fresh decree with no notice given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new order' sounds like a political regime, but it rearranges HELD UNDER A.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving unannounced, with no prior notice or fanfare, is what the word describes.

clue.text: Voting arrangements applied to disabled senior citizen in confinement

parts.note: PR is proportional representation, a voting system

indicators.note: the word senior is put out of order, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ballot provisions extended to a frail pensioner in a care home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disabled senior citizen' reads as one phrase, but 'disabled' rearranges SENIOR; 'citizen in confinement' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone held in jail is a person deprived of liberty, locked up.

clue.text: Move a Turner with backing to alternative gallery

indicators.note: the little word is turned back to front

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: A Turner painting is moved to a different gallery with financial backing.
explanation.walkthrough: THE TATE is London's gallery holding the Turner bequest, which is why 'a Turner' fits the surface; it supplies no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn round, or to move in a cycle, is to revolve, a sense of move.
